questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about the cardiac cycle is correct?
options: During joint diastole, the semilunar valves are open and the atrio-ventricular valves are closed
Atrial systole increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 30 per cent
Atrial systole and ventricular systole occur at the same time
The first heart sound, 'lub', is produced by the closure of the semilunar valves
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: in joint diastole the tricuspid and bicuspid valves are open and the semilunar valves are closed.
(2) Correct: atrial contraction adds about 30% to ventricular filling.
(3) Incorrect: the atria relax while the ventricles contract.
(4) Incorrect: 'lub' comes from closure of the AV valves. 'Dub' comes from closure of the semilunar valves.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: A person of ‘O’ blood group has anti ‘A’ and anti ‘B’ antibodies in his blood plasma.
A person of ‘B’ blood group can’t donate blood to a person of ‘A’ blood group.
Blood group is designated on the basis of the presence of antibodies in the blood plasma.
A person of AB blood group is universal recipient.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: group O has no A or B antigens, so its plasma carries both anti-A and anti-B antibodies.
(2) Correct: B blood has B antigens. The anti-B antibodies in A plasma would attack these cells.
(3) Incorrect: the ABO groups are named after the antigens (A, B) on the RBC surface, not after the antibodies in plasma.
(4) Correct: AB plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so AB is the universal recipient.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of leucocyte is the least abundant in normal human blood, making up only about 0.5-1 per cent of the total WBCs?
questions.explanation:
The normal shares of the total WBC count are:
- Neutrophils: 60-65%
- Lymphocytes: 20-25%
- Monocytes: 6-8%
- Eosinophils: 2-3%
- Basophils: 0.5-1%
Basophils are therefore the least abundant. Eosinophils are also few, but they still outnumber basophils.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Tissue fluid has the same mineral distribution as plasma, but it contains far fewer proteins and almost no formed elements.
Reason (R): As blood passes through capillaries, water and small water-soluble substances move into the intercellular spaces, while the larger proteins and most formed elements remain inside the blood vessels.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Interstitial (tissue) fluid has the same mineral distribution as plasma. It differs from blood mainly in protein content and formed elements.
R is true. Only water and small water-soluble solutes, such as minerals, leave the capillaries. Large proteins and most cells are held back.
This selective movement explains both points in A: minerals match plasma, while proteins and cells are largely absent. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: Most reptiles have a 3-chambered heart. Which of the following reptiles is an exception because it has a 4-chambered heart?

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the cardiac cycle are correct?
(i) The atria relax while the ventricles are in systole.
(ii) The impulse reaches the ventricles via the AVN and AV bundle, and the bundle of His spreads it through the ventricular musculature.
(iii) The semilunar valves open at the very instant ventricular systole begins, before the AV valves close.
(iv) Each ventricle pumps out about 70 mL of blood per cycle.
(v) The second heart sound coincides with closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: atrial diastole coincides with ventricular systole.
(ii) Correct: this is the conduction route described in NCERT.
(iii) Incorrect: the AV valves close first, and the semilunar valves open only after ventricular pressure rises further.
(iv) Correct: about 70 mL per cycle is the stroke volume.
(v) Incorrect: AV valve closure gives the first sound, not the second.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Erythroblastosis foetalis can be prevented by giving anti-Rh antibodies to an Rh-ve mother immediately after the delivery of her first Rh+ve child.
Reason (R): Rh antibodies formed in the mother can never cross into the blood of the foetus.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that giving anti-Rh antibodies to the mother right after the first delivery avoids this condition in later pregnancies.
R is false. In later pregnancies, Rh antibodies from the mother can leak into the foetal blood and destroy the foetal RBCs. This is exactly what causes erythroblastosis foetalis.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: The hepatic portal vein carries blood:
options: From the liver to the intestine
From the heart muscle to the right atrium
From the intestine to the liver before it enters systemic circulation
From the lungs to the liver

The hepatic portal system is a unique vascular link between the digestive tract and the liver.
The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the intestine to the liver. This happens before the blood is delivered to the systemic circulation.
Option (1) reverses the direction of flow.
Option (2) describes coronary drainage, not the portal system.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: Which one of the following animals has a closed circulatory system?
questions.explanation:
NCERT: annelids and chordates have a closed circulatory system, where blood always flows through a closed network of vessels.
The earthworm is an annelid, so it has closed circulation.
The cockroach and prawn are arthropods, and Pila is a mollusc. All three have open circulation with sinuses.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An ECG strip from a healthy person shows 12 QRS complexes in 10 seconds. If the stroke volume of each ventricle is 70 mL, what is the cardiac output?
questions.explanation:
Given: 12 QRS complexes in 10 s, and a stroke volume of 70 mL.
Step 1: Each QRS complex is one beat, so the heart rate is (12/10) × 60 = 72 beats per minute.
Step 2: Cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate.
Substituting: 70 mL × 72 = 5040 mL per minute.
So the cardiac output is 5.04 L/min.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In a standard ECG, ventricular contraction starts shortly after the Q point and marks the beginning of systole.
Statement II: The end of the T-wave marks the end of systole.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The QRS complex starts ventricular depolarisation, and contraction begins shortly after Q, marking the start of systole.
Statement II is correct. The T-wave represents ventricular repolarisation, and its end marks the end of systole.
So the span from just after Q to the end of T corresponds to ventricular systole.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) P-wave
(B) QRS complex
(C) T-wave
(D) First heart sound (lub)
List-II
(i) Closure of tricuspid and bicuspid valves
(ii) Depolarisation of atria
(iii) Repolarisation of ventricles
(iv) Depolarisation of ventricles
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(A) P-wave: electrical excitation (depolarisation) of the atria, so A-ii.
(B) QRS complex: depolarisation of the ventricles, which starts ventricular contraction, so B-iv.
(C) T-wave: the ventricles return to the normal state (repolarisation), so C-iii.
(D) Lub: produced by closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves, so D-i.
Answer: (4)

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Persons with blood group O are called universal donors.
Reason (R): The plasma of blood group O individuals contains neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Group O RBCs carry no A or B antigens, so group O blood can be given to persons of any ABO group.
R is false. The plasma of group O individuals contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies.
The blood group whose plasma lacks both antibodies is AB.

questions.question: Choose the option that correctly gives the average life span of human RBCs and the organ where they are destroyed.

RBCs live for an average of 120 days.
After that they are destroyed in the spleen, which is why the spleen is called the 'graveyard of RBCs'.
Red bone marrow is where RBCs are formed in adults, not where they are destroyed.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A closed circulatory system is considered more advantageous than an open circulatory system.
Reason (R): In a closed circulatory system, the flow of fluid can be more precisely regulated.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

A is true: NCERT states that closed circulation is considered more advantageous.
R is true: in a closed system, blood always stays within a network of vessels, so its flow can be precisely regulated.
R is also the reason NCERT gives for A, so R correctly explains A.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The second heart sound (dub) is produced at the beginning of ventricular diastole.
Reason (R): When the ventricles relax, ventricular pressure falls and the semilunar valves close to prevent backflow of blood into the ventricles.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: dub is associated with closure of the semilunar valves, which happens as ventricular diastole begins.
R is true: relaxation lowers ventricular pressure below that in the aorta and pulmonary artery, so the semilunar valves shut.
The closure described in R is exactly the event that produces dub, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
Statement I: The tunica media is comparatively thin in veins.
Statement II: The neural centre that moderates cardiac function through the autonomic nervous system is located in the cerebellum.

Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

Statement I is correct. NCERT notes that the middle layer (tunica media) is comparatively thin in veins.
Statement II is incorrect. The special neural centre that moderates heart function through the ANS lies in the medulla oblongata, not the cerebellum.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The T-wave of a standard ECG indicates:
options: return of the ventricles from the excited to the normal state
excitation of the atria leading to their contraction
generation of the action potential by the SA node
questions.explanation:
The T-wave represents ventricular repolarisation, that is, the ventricles returning from the excited state to the normal state. The end of the T-wave marks the end of systole.
Depolarisation of the ventricles is shown by the QRS complex, which is the most tempting wrong choice.
Atrial excitation is shown by the P-wave.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The plasma of a person with blood group O contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies.
(ii) A person with blood group B can safely receive blood from group B and group O donors.
(iii) The plasma of a person with blood group A contains anti-A antibodies.
(iv) The plasma of a person with blood group AB has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies.
(v) A person with blood group O can safely receive blood from a group A donor.
(vi) Nearly 80 per cent of humans are Rh positive.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: group O plasma has both anti-A and anti-B.
(ii) Correct: group B can receive from B and O donors.
(iii) Incorrect: group A plasma has anti-B. Anti-A would clump the person's own RBCs.
(iv) Correct: group AB plasma has no antibodies.
(v) Incorrect: the anti-A in group O plasma would clump group A RBCs. Group O can receive only O.
(vi) Correct: nearly 80% of humans are Rh+ve.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A dark reddish-brown scum forms at the site of a cut after some time. According to NCERT, this clot (coagulam) is mainly made of:
options: A network of fibrin threads in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped
A mass of fibrinogen molecules bound together by prothrombin
A layer of aggregated albumin and globulin proteins of plasma
A sheet of living leucocytes held together by calcium ions
questions.explanation:
Key fact: NCERT describes the clot or coagulam as a network of threads called fibrins. Dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped in this network.
Why (1) fits: it states exactly this composition.
Why (2) fails: fibrinogen is the inactive plasma protein that is converted into fibrin. It is not the clot itself, and prothrombin does not bind it.
Albumins help in osmotic balance and are not the clot framework. The trapped cells are dead or damaged, not living leucocytes.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: In the human heart, which valve guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle?
questions.explanation:
The opening between the left atrium and left ventricle is guarded by the bicuspid valve, also called the mitral valve.
The tricuspid valve has three muscular cusps. It guards the right atrio-ventricular opening, so it is the tempting wrong choice.
Semilunar valves guard the openings of the ventricles into the pulmonary artery and the aorta.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cardiac impulse is initiated and conducted further upto ventricle. The correct sequence of conduction of impulse is
options: S A Node → A V Node → Purkinje fiber → A V Bundle
S A Node → Purkinje fiber → A V Node → A V Bundle
S A Node → A V Node → A V Bundle → Purkinje fiber
S A Node → Purkinje fiber → A V Bundle → A V Node
questions.explanation:
The SA node, the pacemaker in the right atrium, starts the impulse. The impulse spreads through the atria to the AV node.
From the AV node it passes into the AV bundle (bundle of His). It then travels down the right and left bundle branches to the Purkinje fibres in the ventricular walls.
Correct order: SA node → AV node → AV bundle → Purkinje fibres.
The Purkinje fibres are the last relay, so any option placing them before the AV node or AV bundle is wrong.
Answer: (3)

I. Secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A red blood cell begins in the right atrium. It completes one round of pulmonary circulation and then one round of systemic circulation, returning to the right atrium. In which order does it pass through the heart valves?
options: Bicuspid valve → aortic semilunar valve → tricuspid valve → pulmonary semilunar valve
Tricuspid valve → pulmonary semilunar valve → bicuspid valve → aortic semilunar valve
Tricuspid valve → bicuspid valve → pulmonary semilunar valve → aortic semilunar valve
Pulmonary semilunar valve → tricuspid valve → aortic semilunar valve → bicuspid valve
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Right atrium → right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.
Step 2: Right ventricle → pulmonary artery through the semilunar valve. Blood goes to the lungs and returns by the pulmonary veins to the left atrium.
Step 3: Left atrium → left ventricle through the bicuspid (mitral) valve.
Step 4: Left ventricle → aorta through the semilunar valve. Blood goes to the tissues and returns via the vena cava to the right atrium.
Answer: (2)

(i) Release factors on injury that activate the clotting mechanism

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A freshly drawn blood sample is immediately mixed with a chemical that binds and removes all free Ca++ ions. The tube is then left undisturbed. What is the most likely observation?
options: The blood clots faster, because fibrinogen changes directly into fibrin without thrombin
The blood clots normally, because Ca++ is needed only for muscle contraction
The blood stays fluid, because the clotting reactions cannot proceed properly without Ca++
All the RBCs are immediately destroyed, releasing haemoglobin that forms a clot
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that calcium ions play a very important role in clotting.
If free Ca++ is removed, the cascade that forms thrombokinase, and then thrombin and fibrin, cannot proceed properly.
Without a fibrin network no clot can form, so the blood stays fluid.
Option (1) is wrong because fibrin forms only through the action of thrombin.
Option (2) wrongly limits Ca++ to muscle contraction.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the human heart are correct?
(i) The walls of the ventricles are much thicker than those of the atria.
(ii) The atria are the larger, lower chambers of the heart.
(iii) The atrio-ventricular septum is made of thick fibrous tissue.
(iv) Semilunar valves are present at the openings of the ventricles into the pulmonary artery and the aorta.
(v) The heart lies in the thoracic cavity, slightly tilted to the right.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: ventricular walls are much thicker than atrial walls.
(ii) Incorrect: the atria are the relatively small upper chambers, and the ventricles are the larger lower chambers.
(iii) Correct: the atrio-ventricular septum is thick fibrous tissue.
(iv) Correct: semilunar valves guard the pulmonary artery and aortic openings.
(v) Incorrect: the heart is tilted slightly to the left.
Three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cardiac activity could be moderated by the autonomous neural system. Tick the correct answer:
options: The parasympathetic system stimulates heart rate and stroke volume
The sympathetic system stimulates heart rate and stroke volume
The parasympathetic system decreases the heart rate but increases stroke volume
The sympathetic system decreases the heart rate but increases stroke volume
questions.explanation:
Neural signals through the sympathetic nerves increase the rate of heartbeat and the strength of ventricular contraction. Stronger contraction raises stroke volume, so cardiac output rises.
Parasympathetic signals (vagus nerve) decrease the heart rate and the speed of conduction, which lowers cardiac output.
Options (1) and (3) give the parasympathetic system stimulating effects it does not have. Option (4) wrongly says sympathetic stimulation lowers heart rate.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about leucocytes are correct?
(i) Neutrophils are the most abundant WBCs.
(ii) Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin.
(iii) Monocytes are granulocytes with phagocytic activity.
(iv) Eosinophils are associated with allergic reactions.
(v) Lymphocytes form about 20-25 per cent of total WBCs.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: neutrophils form 60-65 per cent of total WBCs.
(ii) Correct: basophils secrete these substances and take part in inflammatory reactions.
(iii) Incorrect: monocytes are phagocytic, but they are agranulocytes, not granulocytes.
(iv) Correct: eosinophils resist infections and are linked with allergy.
(v) Correct: lymphocytes make up 20-25 per cent of total WBCs.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following pregnancies carry a risk of erythroblastosis foetalis for the foetus?
(i) Rh+ve mother, Rh-ve foetus
(ii) Rh-ve mother, Rh-ve foetus
(iii) Rh+ve mother, Rh+ve foetus
(iv) Rh-ve mother, Rh+ve foetus, second pregnancy; the mother was exposed at her first Rh+ve delivery and received no anti-Rh antibodies
(v) Rh-ve mother, Rh+ve foetus, second pregnancy; the mother received anti-Rh antibodies immediately after her first delivery
questions.explanation:
(i) No risk: an Rh+ve mother does not make anti-Rh antibodies.
(ii) No risk: the foetus has no Rh antigen to be attacked.
(iii) No risk: both are Rh+ve, so there is no incompatibility.
(iv) Risk: the sensitised Rh-ve mother's antibodies can destroy the RBCs of the Rh+ve foetus.
(v) No risk: the treatment given after the first delivery prevents sensitisation.
Only one case carries risk.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The human heart is described as myogenic.
Reason (R): The normal activities of the heart are auto-regulated by the nodal tissue, which can generate action potentials without any external stimulus.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the heart is called myogenic.
R is true: nodal tissue (SAN, AVN and others) is autoexcitable and regulates the heart intrinsically.
The heart is called myogenic precisely because its beat starts in specialised muscle, not in nerves. So R explains A.
Neural and hormonal signals only moderate this activity.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (features of a standard ECG) with List-II (events they represent).
List-I
(a) P-wave
(b) QRS complex
(c) T-wave
(d) End of T-wave
List-II
(i) Repolarisation of ventricles
(ii) End of ventricular systole
(iii) Depolarisation of atria
(iv) Depolarisation of ventricles
questions.explanation:
(a) The P-wave shows atrial depolarisation, which leads to atrial contraction, so (a)-(iii).
(b) The QRS complex shows ventricular depolarisation, which starts ventricular contraction, so (b)-(iv).
(c) The T-wave shows the ventricles returning to the normal state (repolarisation), so (c)-(i).
(d) The end of the T-wave marks the end of systole, so (d)-(ii).
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The lymphatic system collects interstitial fluid from the tissues and drains it back into the
questions.explanation:
NCERT describes an elaborate network of vessels, the lymphatic system, that collects tissue fluid.
This system drains the fluid back into the major veins, which returns it to the blood circulation.
It does not open into arteries, into a heart chamber directly, or into the hepatic portal vein.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The human heart is described as myogenic because:
options: Its activity is initiated by impulses from the medulla oblongata
Its normal activity is auto-regulated by specialised nodal tissue
It is made of skeletal muscle under voluntary control
Adrenal medullary hormones start each heartbeat
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the normal activities of the heart are regulated intrinsically by specialised muscle, the nodal tissue. That is why the heart is called myogenic.
The medulla oblongata only moderates heart function through the ANS. It does not initiate the beat, so option (1) is wrong.
The heart is made of cardiac muscle, not skeletal muscle.
Hormones can change cardiac output but do not trigger each beat.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Monocytes and neutrophils both belong to the granulocyte category of WBCs.
Statement II: Monocytes and neutrophils are both phagocytic cells that destroy foreign organisms entering the body.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Neutrophils are granulocytes, but monocytes are agranulocytes, along with lymphocytes.
Statement II is correct. NCERT names neutrophils and monocytes as the phagocytic cells that destroy foreign organisms.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) First heart sound

(ii) Closure of semilunar valves

(b) Dub, the second sound, comes from closure of the semilunar valves: (ii).
(c) Stroke volume, the blood pumped by each ventricle per beat, is about 70 mL: (i).
(d) Cardiac output, the blood pumped by each ventricle per minute, is about 5 L: (iii).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to Table 15.1 of NCERT, a recipient with blood group B can safely receive blood from donors of group(s):

Donor blood must therefore lack antigen A. Groups B and O meet this condition.
Groups A and AB carry antigen A, so their RBCs would clump.

questions.question: Coronary artery disease (atherosclerosis) primarily affects which blood vessels?
options: Vessels carrying blood from the intestine to the liver
Vessels carrying blood from the lungs to the left atrium
Vessels supplying blood to the heart muscle
Vessels carrying deoxygenated blood to the lungs
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that CAD affects the vessels that supply blood to the heart muscle. These are the coronary vessels.
Option (1) describes the hepatic portal system.
Options (2) and (4) describe the pulmonary veins and the pulmonary artery.
None of these is the target of CAD.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A marked reduction in the number of platelets in blood can lead to excessive loss of blood after an injury.
Reason (R): Platelets release a variety of substances, most of which are involved in the coagulation of blood.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that a reduction in platelet number can cause clotting disorders, leading to excessive blood loss.
R is true. Platelets release substances that mostly act in blood clotting.
Fewer platelets means less of these clotting substances, so clotting is impaired. R therefore correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A patient's ECG shows normal, regularly spaced P-waves. However, some P-waves are not followed by a QRS complex. The defect most likely lies in:
options: the sino-atrial node, which fails to generate action potentials
the atrial musculature, which fails to depolarise
the conduction of impulses from the atria to the ventricles through the AVN and AV bundle
the semilunar valves, which fail to close
questions.explanation:
Normal P-waves show that the SAN is firing and the atria are depolarising. This rules out the SAN and the atrial muscle.
The QRS complex is ventricular depolarisation, which depends on the impulse being conducted by the AVN, the AV bundle and the bundle of His.
A P-wave without a following QRS therefore means the impulse did not reach the ventricles.
Valve closure produces heart sounds and is not shown as ECG waves.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (blood group) with List-II (antibodies in plasma):
List-I
(a) Group A
(b) Group B
(c) Group AB
(d) Group O
List-II
(i) Nil
(ii) Anti-A and anti-B
(iii) Anti-B
(iv) Anti-A
questions.explanation:
(a) Group A carries antigen A, so its plasma has anti-B, which is (iii).
(b) Group B carries antigen B, so its plasma has anti-A, which is (iv).
(c) Group AB carries both antigens, so its plasma has no antibodies, which is (i).
(d) Group O carries no antigen, so its plasma has anti-A and anti-B, which is (ii).
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Suppose the SAN of a person stops functioning, but the rest of the nodal tissue remains healthy. Based on the properties of nodal tissue described in NCERT, what is the most likely outcome?
options: The heart stops beating permanently, because only the SAN can generate action potentials
The heart continues to beat at a rate higher than 72 per minute
The heart continues to beat rhythmically, but at a slower rate, because other nodal tissue is also autoexcitable but generates fewer action potentials per minute
Only the atria continue to contract, while the ventricles stop
questions.explanation:
All nodal musculature is autoexcitable, meaning it can generate action potentials without any external stimulus.
However, the number of action potentials per minute varies across the nodal system, and the SAN generates the maximum (70-75 per minute).
If the SAN fails, the remaining nodal tissue can still drive the heart, but at a lower rate.
So the heart does not stop, which rules out option (1), and it does not speed up, which rules out option (2).
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A vertebrate's heart has two atria. Its left atrium receives oxygenated blood from both the lungs and the skin, and its right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body. The blood leaving its ventricle has an oxygen content intermediate between the two. Which option correctly identifies the animal and its type of circulation?
questions.explanation:
Oxygenated blood arriving from the skin as well as the lungs points to an amphibian such as the frog.
The intermediate oxygen content in the ventricle shows that blood mixes in a single ventricle. This is incomplete double circulation.
The crocodile has a 4-chambered heart, and the lizard has a single ventricle, so both pairings are wrong.
The shark has only one atrium and single circulation, which does not fit the two atria described.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of white blood cell is both an agranulocyte and phagocytic in nature?
questions.explanation:
The agranulocytes are lymphocytes and monocytes.
The phagocytic WBCs named in NCERT are neutrophils and monocytes.
Only the monocyte appears in both groups.
Neutrophils are phagocytic but are granulocytes. Lymphocytes are agranulocytes but are concerned with immune responses, not phagocytosis.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Formed elements constitute nearly 45 per cent of the blood.
(ii) The average WBC count is 6000-8000 per mm$^3$ of blood.
(iii) Monocytes constitute 20-25 per cent of the total WBCs.
(iv) Blood normally contains 1.5 to 3.5 lakh platelets per mm$^3$.
(v) In most mammals, RBCs are biconcave and lack a nucleus.
(vi) Eosinophils are agranulocytes.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: formed elements are about 45 per cent of blood.
(ii) Correct: the WBC count averages 6000-8000 per mm$^3$.
(iii) Incorrect: monocytes are 6-8 per cent; 20-25 per cent is the figure for lymphocytes.
(iv) Correct: platelets number 1,50,000-3,50,000 per mm$^3$.
(v) Correct: RBCs are biconcave and anucleate in most mammals.
(vi) Incorrect: eosinophils are granulocytes.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Starting from joint diastole, arrange the following events of one cardiac cycle in the correct order:
(A) Semilunar valves are forced open
(B) Tricuspid and bicuspid valves close
(C) Atrial systole
(D) Semilunar valves close
(E) Tricuspid and bicuspid valves are pushed open
questions.explanation:
1. The SAN fires and both atria contract (C).
2. Ventricular systole begins, and the rising pressure closes the AV valves (B).
3. Pressure rises further and forces the semilunar valves open (A).
4. The ventricles relax, pressure falls and the semilunar valves close (D).
5. Pressure falls further, and the AV valves are pushed open by atrial blood (E).
Option (4) wrongly opens the AV valves before the semilunar valves close.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
Statement I: Plasma from which the clotting factors have been removed is called serum.
Statement II: Albumins are the plasma proteins mainly involved in the defence mechanisms of the body.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: plasma without its clotting factors is called serum.
Statement II is incorrect: globulins are mainly involved in defence. Albumins help in osmotic balance.
Fibrinogen, the third major plasma protein, is needed for clotting.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During joint diastole, at the start of the cardiac cycle, what is the state of the heart valves?
options: Tricuspid and bicuspid valves closed; semilunar valves open
Tricuspid and bicuspid valves open; semilunar valves closed
questions.explanation:
In joint diastole all four chambers are relaxed.
The tricuspid and bicuspid valves are open, so blood from the vena cava and pulmonary veins flows through the atria into the ventricles.
The semilunar valves stay closed, which prevents backflow from the aorta and pulmonary artery.
Option (1) is the reverse arrangement, which is seen during the ejection phase of ventricular systole.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the valves of the human heart is incorrect?
options: The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by a valve with three muscular cusps
The first heart sound (lub) is produced by the closure of the semilunar valves
Semilunar valves guard the openings of the ventricles into the pulmonary artery and the aorta
The valve between the left atrium and the left ventricle is called the mitral valve
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the tricuspid valve has three muscular flaps and lies between the right atrium and right ventricle.
(2) Incorrect: the first sound (lub) comes from closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves. Closure of the semilunar valves produces the second sound (dub).
(3) Correct: semilunar valves guard the openings into the pulmonary artery and the aorta.
(4) Correct: the bicuspid valve is also called the mitral valve.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements about coagulation of blood:
Statement I: Thrombin, the enzyme that converts fibrinogen into fibrin, is itself formed from an inactive plasma substance, prothrombin, in a reaction requiring the enzyme complex thrombokinase.
Statement II: Coagulation can be initiated only by factors released from platelets; tissues at the site of injury play no role in starting it.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In plasma, inactive prothrombin is converted into thrombin, and this reaction needs the enzyme complex thrombokinase. Thrombin then converts fibrinogen into fibrin.
Statement II is incorrect. An injury does stimulate platelets to release factors that activate coagulation. However, NCERT also states that factors released by the tissues at the site of injury can initiate coagulation. So platelets are not the only trigger.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The second heart sound (dubb) is associated with the closure of
questions.explanation:
The heart makes two sounds in each cardiac cycle.
First sound, 'lub': the tricuspid and bicuspid (AV) valves close at the start of ventricular systole.
Second sound, 'dub': the semilunar valves at the bases of the aorta and pulmonary artery close at the end of ventricular systole. They close because blood tries to flow back into the ventricles.
Options (1), (3) and (4) name the AV valves, which make 'lub', not 'dub'.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Parasympathetic neural signals reduce the cardiac output.
Reason (R): Parasympathetic signals decrease the rate of heart beat and the speed of conduction of action potential.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that parasympathetic signals, a part of the ANS, lower the cardiac output.
R is true. These signals decrease the heart rate and slow the conduction of action potential.
Cardiac output equals stroke volume multiplied by heart rate. So a lower heart rate directly lowers output, and R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Coagulation of blood can be initiated only by factors released from platelets.
Statement II: Thrombokinase is formed by a series of linked enzymic reactions involving several plasma factors.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Platelets release factors that activate coagulation, but NCERT adds that factors released by tissues at the site of injury can also initiate it. So platelets are not the only trigger.
Statement II is correct. Thrombokinase forms through a cascade process of linked enzymic reactions involving factors present in the plasma in an inactive state.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals have a closed circulatory system?
Earthworm, Cockroach, Frog, Pila (apple snail), Pigeon, Scorpion
questions.explanation:
Closed circulation is found in annelids and chordates; open circulation is found in arthropods and molluscs.
Earthworm (annelid): closed.
Frog and pigeon (chordates): closed.
Cockroach and scorpion (arthropods): open.
Pila (mollusc): open.
So three animals have closed circulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the small intestine, absorbed fats are transported first through which of the following?
options: Blood capillaries of the villi, directly into the hepatic portal vein
Lacteals present in the intestinal villi
Coronary vessels of the intestinal wall
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that fats are absorbed through lymph in the lacteals present in the intestinal villi.
Lacteals are lymph vessels, so fat enters the lymph first, not the blood.
The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the intestine to the liver. Fats do not enter it first, so option (1) is the tempting wrong choice.
Pulmonary veins and coronary vessels have no role in intestinal absorption.
Answer: (2)

Assertion (A): Glucose, amino acids and lipids are found in plasma.

A is false but R is true

questions.question: The RBCs of a person with blood group AB carry which surface antigen(s)?

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Neutrophils

List-II
(i) Associated with allergic reactions

questions.question: Which of the following cells does not exhibit phagocytotic activity

Basophils are not phagocytic. They secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin and take part in inflammatory reactions.

questions.question:
Statement I: In fishes, the blood pumped out by the ventricle of the heart is oxygenated blood.
Statement II: In fishes, blood is oxygenated in the gills and then supplied to the body parts, from where deoxygenated blood returns to the heart.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the ECG are correct?
(i) A standard ECG uses three electrical leads.
(ii) For a detailed evaluation of heart function, multiple leads are attached to the chest region.
(iii) The QRS complex represents repolarisation of the atria.
(iv) For a given lead configuration, ECGs of different individuals have roughly the same shape.
(v) Ventricular contraction begins at the end of the T-wave.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: a standard ECG uses one lead on each wrist and one on the left ankle.
(ii) Correct: chest leads are used for a detailed evaluation.
(iii) Incorrect: the QRS complex is ventricular depolarisation.
(iv) Correct: because shapes are similar, any deviation suggests an abnormality.
(v) Incorrect: the end of the T-wave marks the end of systole, not its start.
That makes three correct statements.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Inter-atrial septum
(b) Inter-ventricular septum
(c) Atrio-ventricular septum
(d) Semilunar valves
List-II
(i) Thick fibrous tissue separating the atrium and ventricle of the same side
(ii) Guard the openings of the ventricles into the pulmonary artery and aorta
(iii) Thin muscular wall
(iv) Thick-walled partition between the two ventricles
questions.explanation:
(a) The inter-atrial septum is a thin muscular wall: (iii).
(b) The inter-ventricular septum is thick-walled and separates the two ventricles: (iv).
(c) The atrio-ventricular septum is thick fibrous tissue between the atrium and ventricle of the same side: (i).
(d) Semilunar valves guard the openings of the ventricles into the pulmonary artery and aorta: (ii).
Option (2) swaps the thin and thick septa.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A glucose molecule is absorbed into a blood capillary of the small intestine. Which sequence correctly traces the route its blood follows until it first reaches the lungs?
options: Intestine → aorta → left atrium → left ventricle → pulmonary vein → lungs
Intestine → hepatic portal vein → liver → vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs
Intestine → vena cava → right atrium → left ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs
Intestine → hepatic portal vein → liver → pulmonary vein → left atrium → lungs
questions.explanation:
Blood from the intestine first goes through the hepatic portal vein to the liver. This happens before it joins systemic circulation.
From the liver, the blood drains into the vena cava and enters the right atrium.
It then passes to the right ventricle, which pumps it into the pulmonary artery towards the lungs.
Option (3) skips the liver and wrongly sends blood from the right atrium to the left ventricle.
Option (4) wrongly uses the pulmonary vein, which carries blood away from the lungs.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(a) Interstitial fluid
(b) Lymph
(c) Lacteals
(d) Major veins
List-II:
(i) Receive the fluid drained by the lymphatic system
(ii) Colourless fluid present inside the lymphatic system
(iii) Fluid in spaces between tissue cells through which exchange occurs
(iv) Lymph vessels in intestinal villi that absorb fats
questions.explanation:
(a) Interstitial fluid is the fluid in the spaces between cells and the medium of exchange, so it matches (iii).
(b) Lymph is the colourless fluid present in the lymphatic system, so it matches (ii).
(c) Lacteals are the lymph vessels in the villi that absorb fats, so they match (iv).
(d) Major veins receive the drained lymph, so they match (i).
Note that interstitial fluid and lymph are similar fluids, but they are named by their location.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about blood coagulation are correct?
(i) Prothrombin is an inactive substance present in plasma.
(ii) Thrombokinase is produced by a single direct reaction from prothrombin.
(iii) The fibrin network of a clot traps dead and damaged formed elements.
(iv) Coagulation can begin only when platelets are stimulated; injured tissues play no role.
(v) Calcium ions play a very important role in clotting.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: NCERT calls prothrombin an inactive substance present in plasma.
(ii) Incorrect: Thrombokinase is formed by a cascade involving many plasma factors. It acts on prothrombin rather than being formed from it.
(iii) Correct: Fibrin threads trap dead and damaged formed elements.
(iv) Incorrect: Factors released by injured tissues can also initiate coagulation.
(v) Correct: Ca++ ions are very important in clotting.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How much haemoglobin is present in every 100 mL of blood of a healthy individual?
questions.explanation:
A healthy individual has 12-16 g of haemoglobin in every 100 mL of blood.
The value 6-8 is the percentage of proteins in plasma, so option (1) is wrong.
The values 20-25 (percentage of lymphocytes among WBCs) and 90-92 (percentage of water in plasma) come from other parts of the chapter.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Neutrophils
(b) Basophils
(c) Eosinophils
(d) Lymphocytes
List-II
(i) Secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin
(ii) Occur as B and T forms responsible for immune responses
(iii) Most abundant WBCs, phagocytic in nature
(iv) Associated with allergic reactions
questions.explanation:
(a) Neutrophils make up 60-65% of WBCs and are phagocytic, so (a)-(iii).
(b) Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin and take part in inflammation, so (b)-(i).
(c) Eosinophils resist infections and are associated with allergic reactions, so (c)-(iv).
(d) Lymphocytes occur as B and T forms and carry out immune responses, so (d)-(ii).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly arranges the types of human leucocytes in decreasing order of their percentage among total WBCs?
questions.explanation:
Recall the NCERT percentages: neutrophils 60-65, lymphocytes 20-25, monocytes 6-8, eosinophils 2-3 and basophils 0.5-1.
Arranging these from highest to lowest gives option (4).
Option (2) wrongly places eosinophils above monocytes.
Option (3) wrongly places monocytes above lymphocytes.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) In fishes, the heart pumps oxygenated blood to the gills.
(ii) In amphibians, the left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the gills, lungs or skin.
(iii) In reptiles other than crocodiles, oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix in the single ventricle.
(iv) In birds, the left ventricle receives deoxygenated blood from the left atrium.
(v) In molluscs, blood pumped by the heart flows through large vessels into open body cavities.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: the fish heart pumps deoxygenated blood, which is oxygenated only in the gills.
(ii) Correct: the right atrium receives deoxygenated blood, while the left atrium receives oxygenated blood.
(iii) Correct: the single ventricle pumps out mixed blood, giving incomplete double circulation.
(iv) Incorrect: in birds the left side carries oxygenated blood. Deoxygenated blood goes from the right atrium to the right ventricle.
(v) Correct: molluscs have open circulation with sinuses.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): A person with blood group AB can receive blood from persons of groups A, B, AB and O.
Reason (R): The plasma of a group AB person contains no anti-A or anti-B antibodies.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT calls AB individuals universal recipients because they can accept blood from all four groups.
R is true: Table 15.1 lists nil antibodies for group AB.
R explains A: with no anti-A or anti-B in the recipient's plasma, the donor RBCs are not clumped, whatever antigen they carry.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The sino-atrial node is called the pacemaker of the human heart.
Reason (R): Among all parts of the nodal tissue, the SAN generates the maximum number of action potentials (70-75 per minute), and so it initiates and maintains the rhythmic contraction of the heart.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT calls the SAN the pacemaker.
R is true: all nodal tissue is autoexcitable, but the SAN fires the most action potentials, 70-75 per minute.
Because the SAN fires fastest, it sets the rhythm of the whole heart. That is exactly why it is called the pacemaker, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A standard ECG of an athlete during light exercise shows 15 QRS complexes in a 12-second strip. Each ventricle pumps out 80 mL of blood per beat. What is this person's cardiac output?
questions.explanation:
Given: 15 QRS complexes in 12 s; stroke volume = 80 mL.
Each QRS complex marks one beat, so heart rate = 15 × (60/12) = 75 beats/min.
Formula: cardiac output = stroke volume × heart rate.
Substituting: 80 mL × 75 = 6000 mL/min.
So cardiac output = 6.0 L/min.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Rh antigen found on human red blood cells gets its name from:
options: The Rhine valley, where it was first detected in human blood
The Rhesus monkey, which has a similar antigen on its RBCs
Rheumatic fever patients, in whom it was first found
The rhombic shape of the antigen molecule
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the Rh antigen is similar to an antigen present in Rhesus monkeys.
The abbreviation 'Rh' comes from 'Rhesus'.
The other options are invented origins and have no basis in the text.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the two statements:
Statement I: Albumins are plasma proteins that help in maintaining osmotic balance.
Statement II: Serum is plasma that still contains all the clotting factors.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Albumins are one of the major plasma proteins and help in osmotic balance.
Statement II is incorrect. Serum is plasma without the clotting factors, not plasma with them.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The atrio-ventricular node lies in the lower left corner of the right atrium, close to the atrio-ventricular septum.
Statement II: The atrio-ventricular bundle emerges on the top of the inter-ventricular septum and immediately divides into a right and a left bundle.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: NCERT places the AVN in the lower left corner of the right atrium, near the atrio-ventricular septum.
Statement II is correct: the AV bundle arises from the AVN and passes through the atrio-ventricular septa.
It emerges on top of the inter-ventricular septum and divides into right and left bundles.
These bundles give rise to the Purkinje fibres.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about tissue fluid and lymph are correct?
(i) Interstitial fluid has the same mineral distribution as plasma.
(ii) Lymph contains large plasma proteins and RBCs in the same amounts as blood.
(iii) Fats are absorbed into lymph through the lacteals of intestinal villi.
(iv) The lymphatic system drains the collected fluid into the major arteries.
(v) Lymph is a colourless fluid containing specialised lymphocytes.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: tissue fluid has the same mineral distribution as plasma.
(ii) Incorrect: the larger proteins and most formed elements stay inside the blood vessels.
(iii) Correct: fats are absorbed into the lacteals present in the intestinal villi.
(iv) Incorrect: lymph is drained back into the major veins, not arteries.
(v) Correct: lymph is colourless and carries lymphocytes.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements about ABO blood grouping:
(i) Antigens are chemicals that can induce an immune response, whereas antibodies are proteins produced in response to antigens.
(ii) A group O person can safely receive blood from persons of any ABO group.
(iii) Clumping during a mismatched transfusion involves destruction of RBCs.
(iv) A group AB person can donate blood only to group AB recipients.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: these are NCERT's definitions of antigen and antibody.
(ii) Incorrect: group O plasma has both anti-A and anti-B, so a group O person can receive only group O blood. O is the universal donor, not the universal recipient.
(iii) Correct: NCERT describes clumping as destruction of RBCs.
(iv) Correct: AB RBCs carry both antigens, so only AB plasma (nil antibodies) accepts them.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The heart of a fish such as Labeo (rohu) consists of:
questions.explanation:
NCERT: fishes have a 2-chambered heart with one atrium and one ventricle.
Two atria with one ventricle is the 3-chambered heart of amphibians and most reptiles.
Two atria with two ventricles is the 4-chambered heart of crocodiles, birds and mammals.
No vertebrate has one atrium with two ventricles.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The tricuspid and bicuspid valves close at the beginning of ventricular systole.
Reason (R): Ventricular contraction raises ventricular pressure, and the attempted backflow of blood into the atria shuts these valves.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The AV valves close as soon as the ventricles begin contracting, and this produces the lub sound.
R is true. NCERT states that the rise in ventricular pressure causes their closure because blood tries to flow back into the atria.
R therefore directly explains A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The enzyme complex thrombokinase directly converts inactive fibrinogen into fibrin threads during clotting.
Statement II: Besides factors released by platelets, factors released by injured tissues can also start coagulation, and calcium ions play a very important role in clotting.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
The clotting sequence is: thrombokinase helps convert prothrombin into thrombin, and thrombin then converts fibrinogen into fibrin.
Statement I is incorrect: thrombokinase does not act on fibrinogen directly. Thrombin does.
Statement II is correct: both platelet factors and tissue factors can start coagulation, and Ca++ ions are essential for it.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which sequence correctly traces the spread of an impulse through the nodal tissue of the human heart, from where it originates to where it reaches the ventricular muscle?
options: AVN → SAN → AV bundle → Purkinje fibres → right and left bundles
SAN → AV bundle → AVN → right and left bundles → Purkinje fibres
SAN → AVN → AV bundle → right and left bundles → Purkinje fibres
SAN → AVN → Purkinje fibres → AV bundle → right and left bundles
questions.explanation:
The impulse originates in the SAN, the pacemaker in the right atrium.
It reaches the AVN, which lies near the atrio-ventricular septum.
From the AVN it travels through the AV bundle (bundle of His) across the atrio-ventricular septum.
At the top of the inter-ventricular septum, the AV bundle divides into right and left bundles.
These branch into Purkinje fibres throughout the ventricular musculature.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: When blood passes through tissue capillaries, some fluid moves out into the spaces between cells. Which components are largely retained inside the blood vessels?
options: Larger proteins and most of the formed elements
questions.explanation:
Water and many small water-soluble substances leave the capillaries and form interstitial (tissue) fluid.
Larger proteins and most formed elements stay behind in the blood vessels.
Minerals, glucose, amino acids and gases are small and soluble, so they pass out.
Option (3) is therefore correct, and the other options list things that do leave the capillaries.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the human heart are correct?
(i) The tricuspid valve is formed of three muscular flaps or cusps.
(ii) The walls of the ventricles are much thicker than those of the atria.
(iii) The atria are the larger, lower chambers of the heart.
(iv) The heart lies between the two lungs, slightly tilted to the right.
(v) Heart valves allow blood to flow from the ventricles back into the atria.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the tricuspid valve has three muscular cusps.
(ii) Correct: ventricular walls are much thicker than atrial walls.
(iii) Incorrect: the atria are the small upper chambers; the ventricles are the larger lower chambers.
(iv) Incorrect: the heart is tilted slightly to the left.
(v) Incorrect: valves allow one-way flow only, from atria to ventricles and from ventricles to the arteries, and prevent backflow.
Two statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The inner lining of both arteries and veins, made of squamous endothelium, is called the:
questions.explanation:
Arteries and veins each have three layers.
The innermost layer is the tunica intima. It is a lining of squamous endothelium.
The tunica media is the middle layer of smooth muscle and elastic fibres, so option (1) is wrong.
The tunica externa is the outer layer of fibrous connective tissue.
The pericardium covers the heart, not the vessels.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (animal) with List-II (type of circulation):
List-I
(a) Fish
(b) Frog
(c) Pigeon
(d) Cockroach
List-II
(i) Open circulation with blood in sinuses
(ii) Single circulation
(iii) Incomplete double circulation
(iv) Double circulation
questions.explanation:
(a) Fish – (ii): the 2-chambered heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills and then to the body. Blood passes through the heart only once per circuit.
(b) Frog – (iii): this amphibian has a 3-chambered heart. Blood mixes in the single ventricle.
(c) Pigeon – (iv): birds have a 4-chambered heart with no mixing of blood. There are two separate pathways.
(d) Cockroach – (i): it is an arthropod, so its blood flows into open sinuses.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An Rh-ve mother is pregnant with an Rh+ve foetus. Why is the foetus in her first pregnancy usually not affected by Rh incompatibility?
options: Foetal RBCs do not carry Rh antigen until after birth
The placenta keeps the maternal and foetal blood well separated
Maternal antibodies are destroyed in the foetal spleen
The mother's blood naturally contains no antibodies at all
questions.explanation:
NCERT explains that in the first pregnancy, the foetal Rh antigens are not exposed to the mother's Rh-ve blood. This is because the placenta keeps the two bloods well separated.
As a result, the mother does not make anti-Rh antibodies during this pregnancy.
Option (1) is wrong because the foetus is already Rh+ve.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: To record a standard ECG, the three electrical leads are attached to which sites on the patient?
options: Both wrists and the right ankle
One to each wrist and the left ankle
Both ankles and the left wrist
Three points on the chest wall
questions.explanation:
For a standard ECG, NCERT describes three leads: one on each wrist and one on the left ankle. These continuously monitor heart activity.
Multiple chest leads are used only for a detailed evaluation, not for the standard ECG.
The right ankle is not one of the standard sites.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the formed elements of human blood is incorrect?
options: In adults, RBCs are formed in the red bone marrow.
A healthy adult man has on average 5 to 5.5 million RBCs per mm$^3$ of blood.
Leucocytes lack a nucleus and generally have a long life span.
RBCs have an average life span of 120 days.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: adult RBCs are produced in the red bone marrow.
(2) Correct: the average RBC count is 5-5.5 million per mm$^3$.
(3) Incorrect: leucocytes are nucleated and generally short lived. It is RBCs that lack a nucleus in most mammals.
(4) Correct: RBCs live about 120 days.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An Rh-ve woman delivers an Rh+ve first child, and she is not given anti-Rh antibodies afterwards. Her second foetus turns out to be Rh-ve. What is the most likely outcome for the second foetus?
options: Severe erythroblastosis foetalis, because the mother is already sensitised
No destruction of foetal RBCs, because they lack the Rh antigen that maternal antibodies target
Destruction of the mother's RBCs by antibodies made by the foetus
Mild anaemia only, because the placenta blocks the antibodies completely
questions.explanation:
The mother probably formed anti-Rh antibodies after being exposed at her first delivery.
These antibodies can leak into the foetal blood, but they act only on RBCs that carry the Rh antigen.
An Rh-ve foetus has no Rh antigen, so its RBCs are not destroyed.
Option (1) ignores the foetus's blood group. Option (4) is wrong because NCERT says the antibodies can leak into foetal blood.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Blood is drawn into a plain glass tube containing no anticoagulant and left to stand. A clot forms, and a clear straw-coloured fluid separates above it. Compared with plasma, this fluid lacks
questions.explanation:
During clotting, fibrinogen is converted into fibrin threads that form the clot.
Other clotting factors are also used up in the clotting process.
The fluid left behind is therefore serum, which is plasma without clotting factors.
Albumins, globulins, glucose and amino acids are not used in the clot, so they remain in serum.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The plasma of a person with blood group A contains anti-B antibodies.
Statement II: Blood of a group A person can be safely transfused into a group B recipient.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: group A plasma carries anti-B (Table 15.1).
Statement II is incorrect: group A RBCs carry antigen A, and the group B recipient's plasma has anti-A. The donated RBCs would clump and be destroyed.
A group B recipient can accept blood only from groups B and O.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A patient with blood group B, Rh negative, received an Rh positive transfusion some years ago. He now needs blood again. Which of the following donors is the safest choice?
questions.explanation:
The patient's plasma has anti-A antibodies, so he can receive ABO groups B or O only. This rules out AB and A donors.
His earlier exposure to Rh+ve blood has made him form anti-Rh antibodies.
These antibodies would attack Rh+ve donor RBCs, so the donor must be Rh negative.
Of the options, only O, Rh negative meets both conditions.
The tempting choice, O Rh positive, fails because of the Rh mismatch.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The atrio-ventricular bundle continues from the AVN, passes through the atrio-ventricular septa and emerges on the top of the inter-ventricular septum, where it divides into right and left bundles.
Statement II: The atrio-ventricular septum completely separates the atrium from the ventricle of the same side, with no opening between them.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. The AV bundle arises from the AVN, crosses the atrio-ventricular septa and emerges on top of the inter-ventricular septum. There it splits into right and left bundles, which give rise to Purkinje fibres.
Statement II is incorrect. Each atrio-ventricular septum has an opening that connects the atrium and ventricle of the same side. This opening is guarded by the tricuspid valve on the right and the bicuspid valve on the left.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are correct about lymph?
(i) It carries nutrients.
(ii) It carries hormones.
(iii) It contains lymphocytes.
(iv) Its protein content is the same as that of blood.
(v) It contains erythrocytes in numbers similar to blood.
(vi) It transports fats absorbed in the intestinal villi.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: lymph is an important carrier of nutrients.
(ii) Correct: lymph also carries hormones.
(iii) Correct: lymph contains specialised lymphocytes.
(iv) Incorrect: larger proteins are retained in the blood vessels, so lymph differs from blood in protein content.
(v) Incorrect: most formed elements, including RBCs, stay in the blood.
(vi) Correct: fats are absorbed through lymph in the lacteals.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 15 · Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly explains a phase/ event in cardiac cycle in a standard electrocardiogram?
options: Time between S and T represents atrial systole.
P-wave indicates beginning of ventricular contraction.
questions.explanation:
In an ECG, the P-wave is atrial depolarisation, which leads to atrial contraction. So (4) is wrong.
The QRS complex is ventricular depolarisation, which starts ventricular contraction. So (2) is correct and (1) is wrong.
The T-wave is ventricular repolarisation, when the ventricles return to normal. The end of the T-wave marks the end of ventricular systole.
The S–T interval belongs to the ventricles, not to atrial systole. So (3) is wrong.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Heart failure
(B) Cardiac arrest
(C) Heart attack
(D) Angina pectoris
List-II
(i) Heart stops beating
(ii) Heart muscle suddenly damaged by inadequate blood supply
(iii) Heart not pumping blood effectively enough to meet the body's needs
(iv) Acute chest pain due to insufficient oxygen reaching heart muscle
questions.explanation:
A-(iii): Heart failure means the heart is not pumping blood effectively enough to meet the body's needs.
B-(i): Cardiac arrest is when the heart stops beating.
C-(ii): A heart attack is sudden damage to heart muscle from inadequate blood supply.
D-(iv): Angina is chest pain due to insufficient oxygen reaching the heart muscle.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Heart failure is sometimes referred to as congestive heart failure.
Reason (R): Congestion of the lungs is one of the main symptoms of heart failure.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: NCERT says heart failure is sometimes called congestive heart failure.
R is true: congestion of the lungs is one of its main symptoms.
R gives the reason for the name 'congestive', so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plasma forms roughly what proportion of human blood?
questions.explanation:
Blood has two parts: the fluid matrix (plasma) and the formed elements.
Plasma makes up nearly 55% of blood. The formed elements make up the remaining ~45%.
90-92% is the water content of plasma, not plasma's share of blood.
6-8% is the protein content of plasma.
